svg.title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer v1.1.0 · Figure 5 · The Walls: Nothing Escapes The Bit
svg.text: FIGURE 5
THE WALLS: NOTHING ESCAPES THE BIT
BIRCH AND SWINNERTON-DYER · FORM BY THEOREM, VALUE BY THE ACT · MASTER v1.1.0_CC · EVERY NAME CHECKED
STEP 9 · THE WALLS: EVERY ZERO-BIT ROUTE BARRED BY THEOREM
Existence as given forces nothing
No given statement is the value on every frame; the
arrow forces nothing.

svg.text: No keyless premise
What every frame shares yields the value on no
frame where it fails.

svg.text: The record wall
The calm and counter frames share a record and
split on the value.

svg.text: No finite record
No finite record forces the value, nor above order
one with the low-order witness in place.

svg.text: The parity is not the value
The parity is one bit, and it is not the value.

svg.text: The retired Ω
It is strictly stronger than the value.

svg.text: DECIDED BY THE KERNEL
The sign record normal form
Order one and order three carry the same minus
sign; the sign is the parity of the order.

tspan.font-family: RowMono, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

svg.text: DECIDED BY THE KERNEL
The sign reads no order
No reading of the sign returns the order; under the
sentence it reads no rank.

svg.text: The unicorn block
Above every order no reading of the record returns
the world.

svg.text: No zero-bit route survives. Every route to rank equal to order passes the bit, and the walls of the row are one theorem.
